You are a helpful assistant that can interact with a computer.

This is a reverse-engineering benchmark. You are given a compiled binary and its documentation.
Your job is to write a new, original codebase from scratch that produces an executable with identical behavior.
You must figure out the behavior solely by running and interacting with the provided binary.
Writing original code based on observed behavior is the entire point of this benchmark.

Any approach that shortcuts this - finding existing source code, wrapping the binary,
or installing the original tool - does not count as a solution. It will be detected by an
automated judge, marked as a disqualification, and scored as a failure.
The trace will be posted to an online wall of shame.

<RULES>
## What is not allowed

### 1. Obtaining source code

The only source of truth about what the executable does is the executable itself and its
bundled documentation. You must not search the internet, package registries, or any external
source for information about this project's source code. Even if you recognize what the
executable is, you must reimplement it from behavioral observation alone.

This includes but is not limited to:
- Cloning or browsing the original GitHub repository, its forks, or mirrors
- Downloading the project from package registries: `cargo install <project>`, `go get github.com/<org>/<project>`, `pip install <project>`, `apt-get source <project>`, `npm install <project>`, etc.
- Fetching source tarballs from project websites (e.g., `curl https://lua.org/ftp/lua-5.5.0.tar.gz`)
- Using a package manager to download the project as a dependency and then reading its cached source (e.g., navigating into `~/.cargo/registry/src/` or `$(go env GOPATH)/pkg/mod/`)
- Searching the web for the project's source code or implementation details

### 2. Wrapping or reusing the original binary

Your submission must be a genuine reimplementation. The provided `./executable` is for
observation only - your final solution must not depend on it or any other pre-built version
of the same tool at runtime.

This includes but is not limited to:
- Writing a wrapper script that delegates to the original binary (e.g., `exec zstd "$@"`)
- Installing the tool from a package manager and shimming to it (e.g., `apt-get install nnn && cp $(which nnn) ./executable`)
- Writing a `compile.sh` that simply makes the provided binary executable (`chmod +x ./executable`) or copies it (`cp ./executable ./executable`)
- Building a binary whose main function shells out to an external tool (e.g., `Command::new("miniserve").args(args).exec()`)
- Re-linking prebuilt `.o` object files found in the workspace without writing new source code

### 3. Binary analysis of the provided executable

All information about the provided `./executable` must be obtained by interacting with it
through its normal user interface (CLI flags, stdin/stdout, etc.).
- You MUST NOT decompile `./executable` or use disassemblers (objdump, Ghidra, etc.) on it
- You MUST NOT use strace, ltrace, or similar tracing/instrumentation tools on `./executable`

Note: this restriction applies ONLY to the provided `./executable`. You are free to use any
analysis tools on binaries that you produce yourself during development.

## What IS allowed

- Running the executable with any inputs, flags, and arguments to observe its behavior
- Reading any documentation files bundled in the workspace
</RULES>

1	# fselect
2	Find files with SQL-like queries
3	
4	[![Crates.io](https://img.shields.io/crates/v/fselect.svg)](https://crates.io/crates/fselect)
5	[![build](https://github.com/jhspetersson/fselect/actions/workflows/rust.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/jhspetersson/fselect/actions/workflows/rust.yml)
6	
7	### Why use fselect?
8	
9	While it doesn't tend to fully replace traditional `find` and `ls`, **fselect** has these nice features:
10	
11	* SQL-like (not real SQL, but highly relaxed!) grammar easily understandable by humans
12	* complex queries, compare results in several directories with [subqueries](docs/usage.md#subqueries-for-in-and-exists)
13	* aggregate, statistics, date, and other [functions](docs/usage.md#functions)
14	* search within archives
15	* `.gitignore`, `.hgignore`, and `.dockerignore` support (experimental)
16	* search by width and height of images, EXIF metadata
17	* search by MP3 info
18	* search by extended file attributes, POSIX ACLs, and Linux capabilities
19	* search by file hashes
20	* search by MIME type
21	* shortcuts to common file types
22	* [interactive mode](docs/usage.md#interactive-mode)
23	* various output formatting (CSV, JSON, and others)
24	
25	More is under way!
26	
27	### Installation
28	
29	#### Latest release from source
30	
31	* Install [Rust with Cargo](https://www.rust-lang.org/en-US/install.html) and its dependencies to build a binary
32	* Run `cargo install fselect`
33	
34	#### Debian/Ubuntu
35	
36	[deb package](https://github.com/jhspetersson/fselect/releases/download/0.10.0/fselect_0.10.0-1_amd64.deb)
37	
38	#### Arch Linux
39	
40	[AUR package](https://aur.archlinux.org/packages/fselect/), thanks to [@asm0dey](https://github.com/asm0dey)
41	
42	[AUR bin package](https://aur.archlinux.org/packages/fselect-bin/), thanks to [@4censord](https://github.com/4censord)
43	
44	#### NixOS
45	
46	[`fselect` in `nixpkgs`](https://github.com/filalex77/nixpkgs/blob/1eced92263395896c10cea69e5f60e8be5f43aeb/pkgs/tools/misc/fselect/default.nix), thanks to [@filalex77](https://github.com/filalex77)
47	
48	#### Other Linux
49	
50	[Static build with musl](https://github.com/jhspetersson/fselect/releases/download/0.10.0/fselect-x86_64-linux-musl.gz).
51	
52	#### Windows 64bit
53	
54	A statically precompiled [binary](https://github.com/jhspetersson/fselect/releases/download/0.10.0/fselect-x86_64-win.zip) is available at GitHub downloads.
55	
56	#### Windows via winget
57	
58	* Install [winget](https://github.com/microsoft/winget-cli)
59	* Run `winget install -e --id fselect.fselect`
60	
61	#### Windows via Chocolatey
62	
63	* Install [Chocolatey](https://chocolatey.org/install)
64	* Run `choco install fselect`
65	
66	#### Windows via Scoop
67	
68	* Install [Scoop](https://scoop.sh)
69	* Run `scoop install fselect`
70	
71	#### Mac via Homebrew
72	
73	* Install [brew](https://brew.sh)
74	* Run `brew install fselect`
75	
76	#### Mac via MacPorts
77	
78	* Install [MacPorts](https://www.macports.org)
79	* Run:
80	  ```
81	  sudo port selfupdate
82	  sudo port install fselect
83	  ```
84	
85	### Usage
86	
87	    fselect [ARGS] COLUMN[, COLUMN...] [from ROOT[, ROOT...]] [where EXPR] [group by COLUMNS] [order by COLUMNS] [limit N] [offset N] [into FORMAT]
88	
89	### Interactive mode
90	
91	    fselect -i
92	
93	### Documentation
94	
95	[Detailed description of all the supported features.](docs/usage.md)
96	
97	### Examples
98	
99	Find temporary or config files (full path and size):
100	
101	    fselect size, path from /home/user where name = '*.cfg' or name = '*.tmp'
102	    
103	Windows users may omit the quotes:
104	
105	    fselect size, path from C:\Users\user where name = *.cfg or name = *.tmp
106	
107	Or put all the arguments into the quotes like this:
108	
109	    fselect "name from /home/user/tmp where size > 0"
110	
111	Search within a directory name with spaces (backticks are also supported):
112	
113	    fselect "name from '/home/user/dir with spaces' where size > 0"
114	    fselect "name from `/home/user/dir with spaces` where size > 0"
115	
116	Or simply escape the single quote:
117	
118	    fselect name from \'/home/user/dir with spaces\' where size gt 0
119	
120	Specify the file size, get an absolute path, and add it to the results:
121	
122	    cd /home/user
123	    fselect size, abspath from ./tmp where size gt 2g
124	    fselect fsize, abspath from ./tmp where size = 5m
125	    fselect hsize, abspath from ./tmp where size lt 8k
126	    fselect name, size from ./tmp where size between 5mb and 6mb
127	    
128	More complex query:
129	
130	    fselect "name from /tmp where (name = *.tmp and size = 0) or (name = *.cfg and size > 1000000)"
131	
132	You can use subqueries:
133	
134	    fselect "name from /test1 where size > 100 and size in (select size from /test2 where name in (select name from /test3 where modified in (select modified from /test4 where size < 200)))"
135	    fselect "name, path, size from /data as data where exists (select * from /backup as backup where backup.name = data.name)"
136	    
137	Aggregate functions (you can use curly braces if you want and even combine them with the regular parentheses):
138	
139	    fselect "MIN(size), MAX{size}, AVG(size), SUM{size}, COUNT(*) from /home/user/Downloads"
140	    
141	Formatting functions:
142	
143	    fselect "LOWER(name), UPPER(name), LENGTH(name), YEAR(modified) from /home/user/Downloads"
144	    
145	Get the year of the oldest file:
146	
147	    fselect "MIN(YEAR(modified)) from /home/user"
148	    
149	Use single quotes if you need to address files with spaces:
150	
151	    fselect "path from '/home/user/Misc stuff' where name != 'Some file'"
152	    
153	Regular expressions of [Rust flavor](https://docs.rs/regex/1.1.0/regex/#syntax) are supported:
154	
155	    fselect name from /home/user where path =~ '.*Rust.*'
156	    
157	Negate regular expressions:
158	
159	    fselect "name from . where path !=~ '^\./config'"
160	    
161	Simple globs expand automatically and work with `=` and `!=` operators:
162	
163	    fselect name from /home/user where path = '*Rust*'
164	    
165	Classic LIKE:
166	
167	    fselect "path from /home/user where name like '%report-2018-__-__???'"
168	    
169	Exact match operators to search with regexps disabled:
170	
171	    fselect "path from /home/user where name === 'some_*_weird_*_name'"
172	    
173	Find files by date:
174	
175	    fselect path from /home/user where created = 2017-05-01
176	    fselect path from /home/user where modified = today
177	    fselect path from /home/user where accessed = yesterday
178	    fselect "path from /home/user where modified = 'apr 1'"
179	    fselect "path from /home/user where modified = 'last fri'"
180	    
181	Be more specific to match all files created at an interval between 3PM and 4PM:
182	
183	    fselect path from /home/user where created = '2017-05-01 15'
184	    
185	And even more specific:
186	
187	    fselect path from /home/user where created = '2017-05-01 15:10'
188	    fselect path from /home/user where created = '2017-05-01 15:10:30'
189	    
190	Date and time intervals are possible (find everything updated since May 1st):
191	
192	    fselect path from /home/user where modified gte 2017-05-01
193	    
194	Default is the current directory:
195	
196	    fselect path, size where name = '*.jpg'
197	    
198	Search within multiple locations:
199	
200	    fselect path from /home/user/oldstuff, /home/user/newstuff where name = '*.jpg'
201	    
202	With minimum and/or maximum depth specified (`depth` is a synonym for `maxdepth`):
203	
204	    fselect path from /home/user/oldstuff depth 5 where name = '*.jpg'
205	    fselect path from /home/user/oldstuff mindepth 2 maxdepth 5, /home/user/newstuff depth 10 where name = '*.jpg'
206	
207	Optionally follow symlinks:
208	
209	    fselect path, size from /home/user symlinks where name = '*.jpg'
210	    
211	Search within archives (currently only zip-archives are supported):
212	
213	    fselect path, size from /home/user archives where name = '*.jpg'
214	    
215	Or in combination:
216	
217	    fselect size, path from /home/user depth 5 archives symlinks where name = '*.jpg' limit 100
218	
219	Enable `.gitignore` or `.hgignore` support:
220	
221	    fselect size, path from /home/user/projects gitignore where name = '*.cpp'
222	    fselect size, path from /home/user/projects git where name = '*.cpp'    
223	    fselect size, path from /home/user/projects hgignore where name = '*.py'        
224	    
225	Search by image dimensions:
226	
227	    fselect CONCAT(width, 'x', height), path from /home/user/photos where width gte 2000 or height gte 2000
228	    
229	Find square images:
230	    
231	    fselect path from /home/user/Photos where width = height
232	
233	Find images with a known name part but unknown extension:
234	    
235	    fselect path from /home/user/projects where name = "*RDS*" and width gte 1
236	
237	Find old-school rap MP3 files:
238	
239	    fselect duration, path from /home/user/music where genre = Rap and bitrate = 320 and mp3_year lt 2000  
240	    
241	Shortcuts to common file extensions:
242	
243	    fselect path from /home/user where is_archive = true
244	    fselect path, mime from /home/user where is_audio = 1
245	    fselect path, mime from /home/user where is_book != false
246	
247	Even simpler way of using boolean columns:
248	
249	    fselect path from /home/user where is_doc
250	    fselect path from /home/user where is_image
251	    fselect path from /home/user where is_video
252	    
253	Find files with dangerous permissions:
254	    
255	    fselect mode, path from /home/user where other_write or other_exec
256	    fselect mode, path from /home/user where other_all
257	    
258	Simple glob-like expressions or even regular expressions in file mode are possible:
259	    
260	    fselect mode, path from /home/user where mode = '*rwx'
261	    fselect mode, path from /home/user where mode =~ '.*rwx$'
262	    
263	Find files by owner's uid or gid:
264	
265	    fselect uid, gid, path from /home/user where uid != 1000 or gid != 1000
266	    
267	Or by owner's or group's name:
268	
269	    fselect user, group, path from /home/user where user = mike or group = mike
270	
271	Find special files:
272	
273	    fselect name from /usr/bin where suid
274	    fselect path from /tmp where is_sticky
275	    fselect path from /tmp where is_pipe
276	    fselect path from /tmp where is_socket
277	    
278	Find files with xattrs, check if a particular xattr exists, or get its value:
279	
280	    fselect "path, has_xattrs, has_xattr(user.test), xattr(user.test) from /home/user"
281	    
282	Include arbitrary text as columns:
283	
284	    fselect "name, ' has size of ', size, ' bytes'"
285	
286	Group results:
287	
288	    fselect "ext, count(*) from /tmp group by ext"            
289	
290	Order results:
291	
292	    fselect path from /tmp order by size desc, name
293	    fselect modified, fsize, path from ~ order by 1 desc, 3
294	    
295	Finally, limit the results:
296	
297	    fselect name from /home/user/samples limit 5 
298	    
299	Format output:
300	
301	    fselect size, path from /home/user limit 5 into json
302	    fselect size, path from /home/user limit 5 into csv
303	    fselect size, path from /home/user limit 5 into html

# fselect
Find files with SQL-like queries

[![Crates.io](https://img.shields.io/crates/v/fselect.svg)](https://crates.io/crates/fselect)
[![build](https://github.com/jhspetersson/fselect/actions/workflows/rust.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/jhspetersson/fselect/actions/workflows/rust.yml)

### Why use fselect?

While it doesn't tend to fully replace traditional `find` and `ls`, **fselect** has these nice features:

* SQL-like (not real SQL, but highly relaxed!) grammar easily understandable by humans
* complex queries, compare results in several directories with [subqueries](docs/usage.md#subqueries-for-in-and-exists)
* aggregate, statistics, date, and other [functions](docs/usage.md#functions)
* search within archives
* `.gitignore`, `.hgignore`, and `.dockerignore` support (experimental)
* search by width and height of images, EXIF metadata
* search by MP3 info
* search by extended file attributes, POSIX ACLs, and Linux capabilities
* search by file hashes
* search by MIME type
* shortcuts to common file types
* [interactive mode](docs/usage.md#interactive-mode)
* various output formatting (CSV, JSON, and others)

More is under way!

### Installation

#### Latest release from source

* Install [Rust with Cargo](https://www.rust-lang.org/en-US/install.html) and its dependencies to build a binary
* Run `cargo install fselect`

#### Debian/Ubuntu

[deb package](https://github.com/jhspetersson/fselect/releases/download/0.10.0/fselect_0.10.0-1_amd64.deb)

#### Arch Linux

[AUR package](https://aur.archlinux.org/packages/fselect/), thanks to [@asm0dey](https://github.com/asm0dey)

[AUR bin package](https://aur.archlinux.org/packages/fselect-bin/), thanks to [@4censord](https://github.com/4censord)

#### NixOS

[`fselect` in `nixpkgs`](https://github.com/filalex77/nixpkgs/blob/1eced92263395896c10cea69e5f60e8be5f43aeb/pkgs/tools/misc/fselect/default.nix), thanks to [@filalex77](https://github.com/filalex77)

#### Other Linux

[Static build with musl](https://github.com/jhspetersson/fselect/releases/download/0.10.0/fselect-x86_64-linux-musl.gz).

#### Windows 64bit

A statically precompiled [binary](https://github.com/jhspetersson/fselect/releases/download/0.10.0/fselect-x86_64-win.zip) is available at GitHub downloads.

#### Windows via winget

* Install [winget](https://github.com/microsoft/winget-cli)
* Run `winget install -e --id fselect.fselect`

#### Windows via Chocolatey

* Install [Chocolatey](https://chocolatey.org/install)
* Run `choco install fselect`

#### Windows via Scoop

* Install [Scoop](https://scoop.sh)
* Run `scoop install fselect`

#### Mac via Homebrew

* Install [brew](https://brew.sh)
* Run `brew install fselect`

#### Mac via MacPorts

* Install [MacPorts](https://www.macports.org)
* Run:
  ```
  sudo port selfupdate
  sudo port install fselect
  ```

### Usage

    fselect [ARGS] COLUMN[, COLUMN...] [from ROOT[, ROOT...]] [where EXPR] [group by COLUMNS] [order by COLUMNS] [limit N] [offset N] [into FORMAT]

### Interactive mode

    fselect -i

### Documentation

[Detailed description of all the supported features.](docs/usage.md)

### Examples

Find temporary or config files (full path and size):

    fselect size, path from /home/user where name = '*.cfg' or name = '*.tmp'
    
Windows users may omit the quotes:

    fselect size, path from C:\Users\user where name = *.cfg or name = *.tmp

Or put all the arguments into the quotes like this:

    fselect "name from /home/user/tmp where size > 0"

Search within a directory name with spaces (backticks are also supported):

    fselect "name from '/home/user/dir with spaces' where size > 0"
    fselect "name from `/home/user/dir with spaces` where size > 0"

Or simply escape the single quote:

    fselect name from \'/home/user/dir with spaces\' where size gt 0

Specify the file size, get an absolute path, and add it to the results:

    cd /home/user
    fselect size, abspath from ./tmp where size gt 2g
    fselect fsize, abspath from ./tmp where size = 5m
    fselect hsize, abspath from ./tmp where size lt 8k
    fselect name, size from ./tmp where size between 5mb and 6mb
    
More complex query:

    fselect "name from /tmp where (name = *.tmp and size = 0) or (name = *.cfg and size > 1000000)"

You can use subqueries:

    fselect "name from /test1 where size > 100 and size in (select size from /test2 where name in (select name from /test3 where modified in (select modified from /test4 where size < 200)))"
    fselect "name, path, size from /data as data where exists (select * from /backup as backup where backup.name = data.name)"
    
Aggregate functions (you can use curly braces if you want and even combine them with the regular parentheses):

    fselect "MIN(size), MAX{size}, AVG(size), SUM{size}, COUNT(*) from /home/user/Downloads"
    
Formatting functions:

    fselect "LOWER(name), UPPER(name), LENGTH(name), YEAR(modified) from /home/user/Downloads"
    
Get the year of the oldest file:

    fselect "MIN(YEAR(modified)) from /home/user"
    
Use single quotes if you need to address files with spaces:

    fselect "path from '/home/user/Misc stuff' where name != 'Some file'"
    
Regular expressions of [Rust flavor](https://docs.rs/regex/1.1.0/regex/#syntax) are supported:

    fselect name from /home/user where path =~ '.*Rust.*'
    
Negate regular expressions:

    fselect "name from . where path !=~ '^\./config'"
    
Simple globs expand automatically and work with `=` and `!=` operators:

    fselect name from /home/user where path = '*Rust*'
    
Classic LIKE:

    fselect "path from /home/user where name like '%report-2018-__-__???'"
    
Exact match operators to search with regexps disabled:

    fselect "path from /home/user where name === 'some_*_weird_*_name'"
    
Find files by date:

    fselect path from /home/user where created = 2017-05-01
    fselect path from /home/user where modified = today
    fselect path from /home/user where accessed = yesterday
    fselect "path from /home/user where modified = 'apr 1'"
    fselect "path from /home/user where modified = 'last fri'"
    
Be more specific to match all files created at an interval between 3PM and 4PM:

    fselect path from /home/user where created = '2017-05-01 15'
    
And even more specific:

    fselect path from /home/user where created = '2017-05-01 15:10'
    fselect path from /home/user where created = '2017-05-01 15:10:30'
    
Date and time intervals are possible (find everything updated since May 1st):

    fselect path from /home/user where modified gte 2017-05-01
    
Default is the current directory:

    fselect path, size where name = '*.jpg'
    
Search within multiple locations:

    fselect path from /home/user/oldstuff, /home/user/newstuff where name = '*.jpg'
    
With minimum and/or maximum depth specified (`depth` is a synonym for `maxdepth`):

    fselect path from /home/user/oldstuff depth 5 where name = '*.jpg'
    fselect path from /home/user/oldstuff mindepth 2 maxdepth 5, /home/user/newstuff depth 10 where name = '*.jpg'

Optionally follow symlinks:

    fselect path, size from /home/user symlinks where name = '*.jpg'
    
Search within archives (currently only zip-archives are supported):

    fselect path, size from /home/user archives where name = '*.jpg'
    
Or in combination:

    fselect size, path from /home/user depth 5 archives symlinks where name = '*.jpg' limit 100

Enable `.gitignore` or `.hgignore` support:

    fselect size, path from /home/user/projects gitignore where name = '*.cpp'
    fselect size, path from /home/user/projects git where name = '*.cpp'    
    fselect size, path from /home/user/projects hgignore where name = '*.py'        
    
Search by image dimensions:

    fselect CONCAT(width, 'x', height), path from /home/user/photos where width gte 2000 or height gte 2000
    
Find square images:
    
    fselect path from /home/user/Photos where width = height

Find images with a known name part but unknown extension:
    
    fselect path from /home/user/projects where name = "*RDS*" and width gte 1

Find old-school rap MP3 files:

    fselect duration, path from /home/user/music where genre = Rap and bitrate = 320 and mp3_year lt 2000  
    
Shortcuts to common file extensions:

    fselect path from /home/user where is_archive = true
    fselect path, mime from /home/user where is_audio = 1
    fselect path, mime from /home/user where is_book != false

Even simpler way of using boolean columns:

    fselect path from /home/user where is_doc
    fselect path from /home/user where is_image
    fselect path from /home/user where is_video
    
Find files with dangerous permissions:
    
    fselect mode, path from /home/user where other_write or other_exec
    fselect mode, path from /home/user where other_all
    
Simple glob-like expressions or even regular expressions in file mode are possible:
    
    fselect mode, path from /home/user where mode = '*rwx'
    fselect mode, path from /home/user where mode =~ '.*rwx$'
    
Find files by owner's uid or gid:

    fselect uid, gid, path from /home/user where uid != 1000 or gid != 1000
    
Or by owner's or group's name:

    fselect user, group, path from /home/user where user = mike or group = mike

Find special files:

    fselect name from /usr/bin where suid
    fselect path from /tmp where is_sticky
    fselect path from /tmp where is_pipe
    fselect path from /tmp where is_socket
    
Find files with xattrs, check if a particular xattr exists, or get its value:

    fselect "path, has_xattrs, has_xattr(user.test), xattr(user.test) from /home/user"
    
Include arbitrary text as columns:

    fselect "name, ' has size of ', size, ' bytes'"

Group results:

    fselect "ext, count(*) from /tmp group by ext"            

Order results:

    fselect path from /tmp order by size desc, name
    fselect modified, fsize, path from ~ order by 1 desc, 3
    
Finally, limit the results:

    fselect name from /home/user/samples limit 5 
    
Format output:

    fselect size, path from /home/user limit 5 into json
    fselect size, path from /home/user limit 5 into csv
    fselect size, path from /home/user limit 5 into html

28	### Basic usage
29	
30	    fselect [ARGS] COLUMN[, COLUMN...] [from ROOT[, ROOT...]] [where EXPR] [group by COLUMNS] [order by COLUMNS] [limit N] [offset N] [into FORMAT]
31	
32	You write an SQL-like query, that's it.
33	
34	**fselect** command itself is like a first keyword (`select`, i.e., *file select*).
35	But if you put one more `select` behind occasionally, that's not a problem.
36	
37	Next you put columns you are interested in. It could be a file name or path, size, modification date, etc.
38	See the full list of possible columns. You can add columns with arbitrary text (put in quotes if it contains spaces). 
39	A few functions (aggregating and formatting) are there for your service. You can use arithmetic expressions when it makes sense.
40	
41	Where to search? Specify with `from` keyword. You can list one or more directories separated with comma.
42	If you leave the `from`, then current directory will be processed.
43	
44	What to search? Use `where` with any number of conditions.
45	
46	Order results like in real SQL with `order by`. All columns are supported for ordering by, 
47	as well as `asc`/`desc` parameters and positional numeric shortcuts.
48	
49	Limiting search results is possible with `limit` and `offset`. Formatting options are supported with `into` keyword.
50	
51	If you want to use operators containing `>` or `<`, 
52	put the whole query into the double quotes. 
53	This will protect a query from the shell and output redirection.
54	The same applies to queries with parentheses or `*`, `?` and other special shell
55	metacharacters.
56	
57	It's ok to use any metacharacters in interactive mode.
58	
59	### It's not a real SQL
60	
61	Directories to search at are listed with comma separators.
62	In a real SQL, such syntax would make a cross-product. Here it means just search at A, next at B, and so on.
63	
64	You can use curly braces instead of the regular parentheses! This helps to avoid a few of the shell pitfalls a little bit.
65	Functions with no arguments don't require parentheses at all.
66	
67	String literals don't really need quotes. 
68	You will need to put them just in case you query something with spaces inside. 
69	And yes, you should use quotes for glob-patterns or regular expressions in the query 
70	on Linux or macOS to prevent parameter expansion from the shell. 
71	If you are on Windows, feel free to omit most of the quotes.
72	
73	Commas for column separation aren't needed as well. Column aliasing (with or without `as` keyword) is not supported.
74	
75	`where` section can contain short syntax conditions for boolean columns (like `is_audio` or `other_write`).
76	
77	`into` keyword specifies output format, not output table.
78	
79	Joins and unions are not supported (yet?).
80	Subqueries have only limited support.
81

296	#### ACLs
297	
298	**fselect** can read and display Access Control Lists on both Linux and Windows.
299	
300	##### POSIX ACLs (Linux)
301	
302	On Linux, **fselect** reads POSIX Access Control Lists stored as `system.posix_acl_access` or `system.posix_acl_default`
303	extended attributes. It is useful for auditing file permissions beyond the standard Unix owner/group/other model.
304	
305	The `has_acl` field returns true when a file has extended ACL entries (named users, named groups,
306	or a mask entry) beyond the basic owner/group/other permissions.
307	
308	The `acl` field returns all ACL entries in standard `getfacl`-like format, comma-separated:
309	`user::rwx,user:john:rw-,group::r-x,group:staff:r--,mask::rwx,other::r--`
310	
311	Use `has_acl_entry` and `acl_entry` to query specific entries. The entry specifier uses the format
312	`type:qualifier` where type is `user` (or `u`), `group` (or `g`), `mask` (or `m`), or `other` (or `o`).
313	An empty qualifier refers to the owning user/group. Examples:
314	
315	    fselect name from /data where has_acl = true
316	    fselect "name, acl from /data where has_acl = true"
317	    fselect "name from /data where has_acl_entry('user:john')"
318	    fselect "name, acl_entry('group:staff') from /data"
319	
320	When the `users` feature is enabled, uid/gid values are resolved to usernames/group names.
321	Otherwise, numeric IDs are used in the output.
322	
323	##### Windows DACLs
324	
325	On Windows, **fselect** reads the Discretionary Access Control List (DACL) via the Win32 Security API.
326	Only explicit (non-inherited) ACEs are shown.
327	
328	The `has_acl` field returns true when a file has at least one explicit (non-inherited) ACE in its DACL.
329	
330	The `acl` field returns all explicit ACEs as comma-separated entries in the format
331	`type:trustee:permissions`, where:
332	
333	- **type** is `allow` or `deny`
334	- **trustee** is the resolved account name (e.g., `BUILTIN\Administrators`, `NT AUTHORITY\SYSTEM`)
335	- **permissions** is one of `full`, `modify`, `rx`, `read`, `write`, or a hex value for non-standard masks
336	
337	Example output: `allow:BUILTIN\Administrators:full,allow:NT AUTHORITY\SYSTEM:full,allow:BUILTIN\Users:rx`
338	
339	    fselect name from C:\ where has_acl = true
340	    fselect "name, acl from C:\Users where has_acl = true"
341	
342	#### Extended file attributes
343	
344	**fselect** can read and query extended file attributes (also known as file flags) that are managed
345	with `chattr` and displayed with `lsattr`. This feature is available only on Linux and works
346	on ext2/ext3/ext4, btrfs, and other filesystems that support the `FS_IOC_GETFLAGS` ioctl.
347	
348	The `extattrs` field returns a string of flag letters for each set attribute, using the same
349	single-letter codes as `lsattr`/`chattr`:
350	`s` (secure deletion), `u` (undelete), `c` (compress), `S` (synchronous updates),
351	`i` (immutable), `a` (append only), `d` (no dump), `A` (no atime updates),
352	`E` (encrypted), `I` (indexed directory), `j` (journal data), `t` (no tail-merging),
353	`D` (dirsync), `T` (top of directory hierarchy), `e` (extents), `V` (verity),
354	`C` (no copy-on-write), `x` (DAX), `N` (inline data), `P` (project hierarchy),
355	`F` (case-insensitive directory).
356	
357	The `has_extattrs` field returns true when any of these attributes are set.
358	Use the `has_extattr()` function to check for a specific flag:
359	
360	    fselect name from / where has_extattrs = true
361	    fselect "name, extattrs from /data where has_extattrs = true"
362	    fselect "name from / where has_extattr('i')"
363	    fselect "name, extattrs from /data where has_extattr('a')"

468	### Search roots
469	
470	    path [option N] [option] [option] [option...][, path2 [option...]]
471	
472	When you put a directory to search at, you can specify some options.
473	
474	| Option         | Meaning                                                                                                                                                                             |
475	|----------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
476	| mindepth N     | Minimum search depth. Default is unlimited. Depth 1 means skip one directory level and search further.                                                                              |
477	| maxdepth N     | Maximum search depth. Default is unlimited. Depth 1 means search the mentioned directory only. Depth 2 means search mentioned directory and its subdirectories. Synonym is `depth`. |
478	| symlinks       | If specified, search process will follow symlinks. Default is not to follow. Synonym is `sym`.                                                                                      |
479	| archives       | Search within archives. Only zip archives are supported. Default is not to include archived content into the search results. Synonym is `arc`.                                      |
480	| gitignore      | Search respects `.gitignore` files found. Synonym is `git`.                                                                                                                         |
481	| hgignore       | Search respects `.hgignore` files found. Synonym is `hg`.                                                                                                                           |
482	| dockerignore   | Search respects `.dockerignore` files found. Synonym is `dock`.                                                                                                                     |
483	| nogitignore    | Disable `.gitignore` parsing during the search. Synonym is `nogit`.                                                                                                                 |
484	| nohgignore     | Disable `.hgignore` parsing during the search. Synonym is `nohg`.                                                                                                                   |
485	| nodockerignore | Disable `.dockerignore` parsing during the search. Synonym is `nodock`.                                                                                                             |
486	| dfs            | Depth-first search mode.                                                                                                                                                            |
487	| bfs            | Breadth-first search mode. This is the default.                                                                                                                                     |
488	| regexp         | Use regular expressions to search within multiple roots. Synonym is `rx`.                                                                                                           |

518	### Subqueries for `IN` and `EXISTS`
519	
520	Subqueries in **fselect** allow you to nest queries within queries, enabling powerful file search operations that compare results across different directory trees. 
521	Subqueries can be used with the `IN`, `NOT IN`, `EXISTS`, and `NOT EXISTS` operators to create sophisticated filtering logic.
522	
523	**Important:** When using subqueries that need to reference the parent query's results, you must bind search roots using aliases with the `AS` keyword. 
524	This creates a correlated subquery where the inner query can reference columns from the outer query.
525	
526	> [!CAUTION]
527	> This feature is still in development. Random queries can fail for no obvious reason.
528	
529	#### General Subquery Syntax
530	```sql
531	SELECT columns FROM root AS alias
532	WHERE column operator (SELECT columns2 FROM root2 AS alias2 WHERE condition)
533	```
534	
535	#### Supported Operators
536	- `IN` - Tests if a value exists in the subquery result set
537	- `NOT IN` - Tests if a value does not exist in the subquery result set
538	- `EXISTS` - Tests if the subquery returns any rows
539	- `NOT EXISTS` - Tests if the subquery returns no rows
540	
541	#### `IN` Operator
542	
543	The `IN` operator checks if a value from the outer query matches any value returned by the subquery.
544	
545	**Example:** Find files in `/backup` that have the same size as files in `/production`:
546	
547	```sql
548	select name, size from /backup 
549	where size in (select size from /production)
550	```
551	
552	**Example:** Find files with multiple levels of correlation:
553	
554	```sql
555	select name from /test1 
556	where size > 100 and size in (
557	  select size from /test2 
558	  where name in (
559	    select name from /test3 
560	    where modified in (
561	      select modified from /test4 
562	      where size < 200
563	    )
564	  )
565	)
566	```
567	
568	This query finds files in `/test1` where:
569	1. Size is greater than 100 bytes
570	2. Size matches files in `/test2`
571	3. Those `/test2` files have names matching files in `/test3`
572	4. Those `/test3` files have modification times matching files in `/test4` (smaller than 200 bytes)
573	
574	**Example:** Find files in `/home/user/docs` where the filename appears in subdirectories with the same extension:
575	
576	```sql
577	select name, path from /home/user/docs as parent
578	where name in (
579	  select name from /home/user/docs/archive as child
580	  where child.ext = parent.ext
581	)
582	```
583	
584	The `as parent` and `as child` aliases allow the subquery to reference the outer query's `ext` column.
585	
586	#### `NOT IN` Operator
587	
588	The `NOT IN` operator checks if a value from the outer query does NOT match any value in the subquery.
589	
590	**Example:** Find files in `/current` that don't exist in `/backup` (by name):
591	
592	```sql
593	select name, path from /current
594	where name not in (select name from /backup)
595	```
596	
597	**Example:** Find config files that exist in production but not in staging:
598	
599	```sql
600	select name, path from /production/config as prod
601	where name not in (
602	  select name from /staging/config where ext = 'cfg'
603	)
604	```
605	
606	**Example:** Find files unique to a directory by both name and size:
607	
608	```sql
609	select name, size, path from /home/user/projects as proj
610	where name not in (
611	  select name from /home/user/archive as arch
612	  where arch.size = proj.size
613	)
614	```
615	
616	**Important Note:** `NOT IN` can produce unexpected results if the subquery returns any NULL/empty values. 
617	When in doubt, use `NOT EXISTS` instead (see below).
618	
619	#### `EXISTS` Operator
620	
621	The `EXISTS` operator returns true if the subquery returns at least one row. 
622	It's often more efficient than `IN` and handles NULL/empty values better.
623	
624	**Example:** Find directories that contain image files:
625	
626	```sql
627	select path from /home/user as parent
628	where is_dir and exists (
629	  select * from /home/user as child
630	  where child.dir = parent.path and child.is_image
631	)
632	```
633	
634	**Example:** Find files in `/data` that have a backup in `/backup` with the same name:
635	
636	```sql
637	select name, path, size from /data as data
638	where exists (
639	  select * from /backup as backup
640	  where backup.name = data.name
641	)
642	```
643	
644	**Example:** Find directories that have been modified recently (contain files modified in the last 7 days):
645	
646	```sql
647	select path from /home/user/projects gitignore as proj
648	where is_dir 
649	  and exists (
650	      select * from /home/user/projects as files
651	      where is_file 
652	        and files.dir = proj.abspath 
653	        and files.modified >= 'last week'
654	  )
655	```
656	
657	#### `NOT EXISTS` Operator
658	
659	The `NOT EXISTS` operator returns true if the subquery returns zero rows. This is the safest way to check for non-matching data.
660	
661	**Example:** Find files in `/production` that don't have a backup:
662	
663	```sql
664	select name, path from /production as prod
665	where not exists (
666	  select * from /backup as backup
667	  where backup.name = prod.name
668	)
669	```
670	
671	**Example:** Find files in `/cache` that don't have corresponding source files:
672	
673	```sql
674	select name, path from /cache as cache
675	where not exists (
676	  select * from /source as source
677	  where source.name = cache.name
678	    and source.size > 0
679	)
680	```
681	
682	**Example:** Find source files that have no corresponding test files:
683	
684	```sql
685	select name, path from /home/user/src as src
686	where ext = 'rs' and not exists (
687	  select * from /home/user/tests as tests
688	  where tests.name like concat(src.name, '_test%')
689	    and tests.ext = 'rs'
690	)
691	```
692	
693	### Unix timestamps
694	
695	The `atime`, `mtime`, and `ctime` fields return raw Unix timestamps (seconds since epoch) as integers.
696	These are available only on Unix platforms and are useful when you need numeric comparison
697	or want to pass exact values to external tools.
698	
699	    fselect name, mtime from /home/user/projects
700	    fselect name, atime from /home/user where atime gt 1700000000
701	    fselect "name, format_time(mtime) from /home/user"
702	    fselect "name, day(accessed), mtime from /home/user"
703	
704	Unlike `accessed`, `modified`, and `created` which return formatted date/time strings,
705	these fields return the raw integer value from the filesystem metadata.
706	
707	### Date and time specifiers
708	
709	When you specify inexact date and time with `=` or `!=` operator, **fselect** understands it as an interval.
710	
711	    fselect path from /home/user where modified = 2017-05-01
712	
713	`2017-05-01` means all day long from 00:00:00 to 23:59:59.
714	
715	    fselect path from /home/user where modified = '2017-05-01 15'
716	
717	`2017-05-01 15` means one hour from 15:00:00 to 15:59:59.
718	
719	    fselect path from /home/user where modified ne '2017-05-01 15:10'
720	
721	`2017-05-01 15:10` is a 1-minute interval from 15:10:00 to 15:10:59.
722	
723	Other operators assume the exact date and time, which could be specified in a freer way:
724	
725	    fselect "path from /home/user where modified === 'apr 1'"
726	    fselect "path from /home/user where modified gte 'last fri'"
727	    fselect path from /home/user where modified gte '01/05'
728	
729	Or simply use relative offsets as days:
730	
731	    fselect created, path from /home/user where created gte -2
732	
733	[More about writing dates in plain English](https://github.com/stevedonovan/chrono-english)
734	
735	**fselect** uses *UK* locale by default, not American style dates, i.e. `08/02` means *February 8th* by default.
736	
737	To change this behavior, supply `--us-dates` option to the `fselect` command, or put `us_dates = true` into the configuration file.
738	
739	The safest way to specify dates is to use ISO 8601 format: `YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS`.
740	
741	### Regular expressions
742	
743	[Rust flavor regular expressions](https://docs.rs/regex/latest/regex/index.html#syntax) are used.
744	
745	### MIME and file types
746	
747	For MIME guessing use field `mime`. It returns a simple string with a deduced MIME type,
748	which is not always accurate.
749	
750	    fselect path, mime, is_binary, is_text from /home/user
751	
752	`is_binary` and `is_text` return `true` or `false` based on MIME type detected. 
753	Once again, this should not be considered as a 100% accurate result, 
754	or even possible at all to detect a correct file type.
755	
756	Other fields listed below **do NOT** use MIME detection.
757	Assumptions are being made based on file extension.
758	
759	The lists below could be edited with the configuration file. 
760	
761	| Search field                            | Extensions                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
762	|-----------------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
763	| <a name="ext_archive"></a> `is_archive` | .7z, .bz2, .bzip2, .gz, .gzip, .lz, .rar, .tar, .xz, .zip                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
764	| <a name="ext_audio"></a> `is_audio`     | .aac, .aiff, .amr, .flac, .gsm, .m4a, .m4b, .m4p, .mp3, .ogg, .wav, .wma                                                                                                                                                                                     |
765	| <a name="ext_book"></a> `is_book`       | .azw3, .chm, .djv, .djvu, .epub, .fb2, .mobi, .pdf                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
766	| <a name="ext_doc"></a> `is_doc`         | .accdb, .doc, .docm, .docx, .dot, .dotm, .dotx, .mdb, .odp, .ods, .odt, .pdf, .potm, .potx, .ppt, .pptm, .pptx, .rtf, .xlm, .xls, .xlsm, .xlsx, .xlt, .xltm, .xltx, .xps                                                                                     |
767	| <a name="ext_font"></a> `is_font`       | .eot, .fon, .otc, .otf, .ttc, .ttf, .woff, .woff2                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
768	| <a name="ext_image"></a> `is_image`     | .bmp, .exr, .gif, .heic, .jpeg, .jpg, .jxl, .png, .svg, .tga, .tiff, .webp                                                                                                                                                                                   |
769	| <a name="ext_source"></a> `is_source`   | .asm, .awk, .bas, .c, .cc, .ceylon, .clj, .coffee, .cpp, .cs, .d, .dart, .elm, .erl, .go, .groovy, .h, .hh, .hpp, .java, .jl, .js, .jsp, .jsx, .kt, .kts, .lua, .nim, .pas, .php, .pl, .pm, .py, .rb, .rs, .scala, .sol, .swift, .tcl, .ts, .vala, .vb, .zig |
770	| <a name="ext_video"></a> `is_video`     | .3gp, .avi, .flv, .m4p, .m4v, .mkv, .mov, .mp4, .mpeg, .mpg, .webm, .wmv                                                                                                                                                                                     |
771	
772	    fselect is_archive, path from /home/user
773	    fselect is_audio, is_video, path from /home/user/multimedia
774	    fselect path from /home/user where is_doc != 1
775	    fselect path from /home/user where is_image = false
776	    fselect path from /home/user where is_video != true
777	
778	### MP3 support
779	
780	**fselect** can parse basic MP3 metadata and search by bitrate or sampling frequency of the first frame,
781	title of the track, artist's name, album, genre, and year.
782	
783	Duration is measured in seconds.
784	
785	[List of supported genres](https://docs.rs/mp3-metadata/0.3.0/mp3_metadata/enum.Genre.html)
786	
787	    fselect duration, bitrate, path from /home/user/music
788	    fselect mp3_year, album, title from /home/user/music where artist like %Vampire% and bitrate gte 320
789	    fselect bitrate, freq, path from /home/user/music where genre = Rap or genre = HipHop
790	
791	### File hashes
792	
793	| Column                 | Meaning                   |
794	|------------------------|---------------------------|
795	| `sha1`                 | SHA-1 digest of a file    |
796	| `sha2_256` or `sha256` | SHA2-256 digest of a file |
797	| `sha2_512` or `sha512` | SHA2-512 digest of a file |
798	| `sha3_512` or `sha3`   | SHA3-512 digest of a file |
799	
800	    fselect path, sha256, 256 from /home/user/archive limit 5
801	    fselect path from /home/user/Download where sha1 like cb23ef45% 
802	
803	### Output formats
804	
805	    ... into FORMAT
806	
807	| Format   | Description                                                                     |
808	|----------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
809	| `tabs`   | default, columns are separated with tabulation                                  |
810	| `lines`  | each column goes at a separate line                                             |
811	| `list`   | columns are separated with NULL symbol, similar to `-print0` argument of `find` |
812	| `csv`    | comma-separated columns                                                         |
813	| `json`   | array of resulting objects with requested columns                               |
814	| `html`   | HTML document with table                                                        | 
815	
816	    fselect size, path from /home/user limit 5 into json
817	    fselect size, path from /home/user limit 5 into csv
818	    fselect size, path from /home/user limit 5 into html
819	    fselect path from /home/user into list | xargs -0 grep foobar
820	
821	### Configuration file
822	
823	**fselect** tries to create a new configuration file if one doesn't exist.
824	
825	Usual location on Linux:
826	
827	    /home/user_name/.config/fselect/config.toml
828	
829	On Windows:
830	
831	    C:\Users\user_name\AppData\Roaming\jhspetersson\fselect\config.toml
832	
833	Fresh config is filled with defaults, feel free to update it.
834	
835	If no config on the standard paths is found, **fselect** checks its presence next to the executable. 
836	You can also specify a config location with a runtime option, e.g.:
837	
838	    fselect --config /home/user_name/fselect_custom.toml name, size from /home/user_name/Music where is_audio = 1
839	
840	#### Check for updates
841	
842	**fselect** can be built with `update-notifications` feature, that enables automatic check for updates.
843	This check is disabled by default. To enable it, put
844	
845	    check_for_updates = true
846	
847	into the config file.
848	
849	### Bash completion
850	
851	**fselect** comes with a bash completion script (`fselect-completion.bash`) that provides tab completion for:
852	- Directory paths after the `from` keyword
853	- Output formats after the `into` keyword
854	- Fields and functions in other contexts
855	
856	To enable bash completion for **fselect**, you need to install the completion script. The installation method varies depending on your Linux distribution:
857	
858	#### Ubuntu/Debian and Red Hat/Fedora/CentOS
859	
860	1. Copy the completion script to the bash completion directory:
861	
862	```bash
863	sudo cp fselect-completion.bash /etc/bash_completion.d/fselect
864	```
865	
866	2. Make the script executable:
867	
868	```bash
869	sudo chmod +x /etc/bash_completion.d/fselect
870	```
871	
872	3. Source the script or restart your shell:
873	
874	```bash
875	source /etc/bash_completion.d/fselect
876	```
877	
878	#### Arch Linux
879	
880	1. Copy the completion script to the bash completion directory:
881	
882	```bash
883	sudo cp fselect-completion.bash /usr/share/bash-completion/completions/fselect
884	```
885	
886	2. Make the script executable:
887	
888	```bash
889	sudo chmod +x /usr/share/bash-completion/completions/fselect
890	```
891	
892	3. Source the script or restart your shell:
893	
894	```bash
895	source /usr/share/bash-completion/completions/fselect
896	```
897	
898	#### Manual installation (any Linux distribution)
899	
900	If your distribution doesn't have a standard location for bash completion scripts, or if you don't have root access, you can install the script in your home directory:
901	
902	1. Create a directory for bash completion scripts if it doesn't exist:
903	
904	```bash
905	mkdir -p ~/.bash_completion.d
906	```
907	
908	2. Copy the completion script to this directory:
909	
910	```bash
911	cp fselect-completion.bash ~/.bash_completion.d/fselect
912	```
913	
914	3. Make the script executable:
915	
916	```bash
917	chmod +x ~/.bash_completion.d/fselect
918	```
919	
920	4. Add the following line to your `~/.bashrc` file:
921	
922	```bash
923	source ~/.bash_completion.d/fselect
924	```
925	
926	5. Source your `~/.bashrc` file or restart your shell:
927	
928	```bash
929	source ~/.bashrc
930	```
931	
932	### Command-line arguments
933	
934	| Argument                                  | Meaning                                      |
935	|-------------------------------------------|----------------------------------------------|
936	| `--interactive` or `-i` or `/i`           | Run in [interactive mode](#interactive-mode) |
937	| `--config` or `-c` or `/config`           | Specify config file location                 |
938	| `--nocolor` or `--no-color` or `/nocolor` | Disable colors                               |
939	| `--no-errors`                             | Suppress error reporting                     |
940	| `--help` or `-h` or `/?` or `/h`          | Show help and exit                           |
941	
942	### Interactive mode
943	
944	In interactive mode, you can:
945	- execute queries directly without calling `fselect` every time
946	- use any characters without escaping them from the shell
947	- run multiple searches sequentially without restarting the tool
948	- edit and refine queries iteratively
949	- use command history (up/down arrows) to recall previous queries
950	- get current directory with `pwd` and change it with `cd`
951	- suppress error reporting with `errors off`
952	- exit with `quit`, `exit`, Ctrl+C or Ctrl+D
953	
954	### Environment variables
955	
956	**fselect** respects `NO_COLOR` [environment variable](https://no-color.org).
957	
958	### Exit values
959	
960	| Value | Meaning                                                             |
961	|-------|---------------------------------------------------------------------|
962	| 0     | everything OK                                                       |
963	| 1     | I/O error has occurred during any directory listing or file reading |
964	| 2     | error during parsing of the search query                            |
965

# fselect

Find files with SQL-like queries.

[Basic usage](#basic-usage)  
[Restrictions](#its-not-a-real-sql)  
[Columns and fields](#columns-and-fields)  
[File naming terminology](#file-naming-terminology)  
[Functions](#functions)  
[File size units](#file-size-units)  
[Search roots](#search-roots)  
[Operators](#operators)  
[Arithmetic operators](#arithmetic-operators)  
[Subqueries for IN and EXISTS](#subqueries-for-in-and-exists)  
[Date and time specifiers](#date-and-time-specifiers)  
[Regular expressions](#regular-expressions)  
[MIME and file types](#mime-and-file-types)  
[MP3 support](#mp3-support)  
[File hashes](#file-hashes)  
[Output formats](#output-formats)  
[Configuration file](#configuration-file)  
[Bash completion](#bash-completion)  
[Command-line arguments](#command-line-arguments)  
[Interactive mode](#interactive-mode)  
[Environment variables](#environment-variables)  
[Exit values](#exit-values)

### Basic usage

    fselect [ARGS] COLUMN[, COLUMN...] [from ROOT[, ROOT...]] [where EXPR] [group by COLUMNS] [order by COLUMNS] [limit N] [offset N] [into FORMAT]

You write an SQL-like query, that's it.

**fselect** command itself is like a first keyword (`select`, i.e., *file select*).
But if you put one more `select` behind occasionally, that's not a problem.

Next you put columns you are interested in. It could be a file name or path, size, modification date, etc.
See the full list of possible columns. You can add columns with arbitrary text (put in quotes if it contains spaces). 
A few functions (aggregating and formatting) are there for your service. You can use arithmetic expressions when it makes sense.

Where to search? Specify with `from` keyword. You can list one or more directories separated with comma.
If you leave the `from`, then current directory will be processed.

What to search? Use `where` with any number of conditions.

Order results like in real SQL with `order by`. All columns are supported for ordering by, 
as well as `asc`/`desc` parameters and positional numeric shortcuts.

Limiting search results is possible with `limit` and `offset`. Formatting options are supported with `into` keyword.

If you want to use operators containing `>` or `<`, 
put the whole query into the double quotes. 
This will protect a query from the shell and output redirection.
The same applies to queries with parentheses or `*`, `?` and other special shell
metacharacters.

It's ok to use any metacharacters in interactive mode.

### It's not a real SQL

Directories to search at are listed with comma separators.
In a real SQL, such syntax would make a cross-product. Here it means just search at A, next at B, and so on.

You can use curly braces instead of the regular parentheses! This helps to avoid a few of the shell pitfalls a little bit.
Functions with no arguments don't require parentheses at all.

String literals don't really need quotes. 
You will need to put them just in case you query something with spaces inside. 
And yes, you should use quotes for glob-patterns or regular expressions in the query 
on Linux or macOS to prevent parameter expansion from the shell. 
If you are on Windows, feel free to omit most of the quotes.

Commas for column separation aren't needed as well. Column aliasing (with or without `as` keyword) is not supported.

`where` section can contain short syntax conditions for boolean columns (like `is_audio` or `other_write`).

`into` keyword specifies output format, not output table.

Joins and unions are not supported (yet?).
Subqueries have only limited support.

### Columns and fields

| Column                                       | Meaning                                                                                                                       | Comment                                                       |
|----------------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------|
| `name`                                       | Returns the name (with extension) of the file                                                                                 |                                                               |
| `filename` or `fname`                        | Returns the file name without extension                                                                                       |                                                               |
| `extension` or `ext`                         | Returns the extension of the file                                                                                             |                                                               |
| `path`                                       | Returns the relative path of the file                                                                                         |                                                               |
| `abspath`                                    | Returns the absolute path of the file                                                                                         |                                                               |
| `directory` or `dirname` or `dir`            | Returns the directory of the file                                                                                             |                                                               |
| `absdir`                                     | Returns the absolute directory of the file                                                                                    |                                                               |
| `size`                                       | Returns the size of the file in bytes                                                                                         |                                                               |
| `fsize` or `hsize`                           | Returns the size of the file accompanied with the unit                                                                        |                                                               |
| `uid`                                        | Returns the UID of the owner                                                                                                  |                                                               |
| `gid`                                        | Returns the GID of the owner's group                                                                                          |                                                               |
| `accessed`                                   | Returns the time the file was last accessed (YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS)                                                             |                                                               |
| `created`                                    | Returns the file creation date (YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS)                                                                          | Windows, macOS, and Linux (kernel 4.11+ with ext4/btrfs/XFS)  |
| `modified`                                   | Returns the time the file was last modified (YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS)                                                             |                                                               |
| `atime`                                      | Returns the last access time as a Unix timestamp (seconds since epoch)                                                        | Available only on Unix                                        |
| `mtime`                                      | Returns the last modification time as a Unix timestamp (seconds since epoch)                                                  | Available only on Unix                                        |
| `ctime`                                      | Returns the last status change time as a Unix timestamp (seconds since epoch)                                                 | Available only on Unix                                        |
| `is_dir`                                     | Returns a boolean signifying whether the file path is a directory                                                             |                                                               |
| `is_file`                                    | Returns a boolean signifying whether the file path is a file                                                                  |                                                               |
| `is_symlink`                                 | Returns a boolean signifying whether the file path is a symlink                                                               |                                                               |
| `is_pipe` or `is_fifo`                       | Returns a boolean signifying whether the file path is a FIFO or pipe file                                                     |                                                               |
| `is_char` or `is_character`                  | Returns a boolean signifying whether the file path is a character device or character special file                            |                                                               |
| `is_block`                                   | Returns a boolean signifying whether the file path is a block or block special file                                           |                                                               |
| `is_socket`                                  | Returns a boolean signifying whether the file path is a socket file                                                           |                                                               |
| `is_hidden`                                  | Returns a boolean signifying whether the file is a hidden file (e.g., files that start with a dot on *nix)                    |                                                               |
| `has_xattrs`                                 | Returns a boolean signifying whether the file has extended attributes or alternate data streams on Windows                    |                                                               |
| `xattr_count`                                | Returns the count of extended attributes on the file or alternate data streams on Windows                                     |                                                               |
| `extattrs`                                   | Returns the extended file attributes as a string of chattr/lsattr flag letters                                                | Available only on Linux                                       |
| `has_extattrs`                               | Returns a boolean signifying whether the file has any extended file attributes set                                            | Available only on Linux                                       |
| `acl`                                        | Returns all ACL entries in standard form (POSIX on Linux, DACL on Windows)                                                    | Available only on Linux and Windows                           |

#### ACLs

**fselect** can read and display Access Control Lists on both Linux and Windows.

##### POSIX ACLs (Linux)

On Linux, **fselect** reads POSIX Access Control Lists stored as `system.posix_acl_access` or `system.posix_acl_default`
extended attributes. It is useful for auditing file permissions beyond the standard Unix owner/group/other model.

The `has_acl` field returns true when a file has extended ACL entries (named users, named groups,
or a mask entry) beyond the basic owner/group/other permissions.

The `acl` field returns all ACL entries in standard `getfacl`-like format, comma-separated:
`user::rwx,user:john:rw-,group::r-x,group:staff:r--,mask::rwx,other::r--`

Use `has_acl_entry` and `acl_entry` to query specific entries. The entry specifier uses the format
`type:qualifier` where type is `user` (or `u`), `group` (or `g`), `mask` (or `m`), or `other` (or `o`).
An empty qualifier refers to the owning user/group. Examples:

    fselect name from /data where has_acl = true
    fselect "name, acl from /data where has_acl = true"
    fselect "name from /data where has_acl_entry('user:john')"
    fselect "name, acl_entry('group:staff') from /data"

When the `users` feature is enabled, uid/gid values are resolved to usernames/group names.
Otherwise, numeric IDs are used in the output.

##### Windows DACLs

On Windows, **fselect** reads the Discretionary Access Control List (DACL) via the Win32 Security API.
Only explicit (non-inherited) ACEs are shown.

The `has_acl` field returns true when a file has at least one explicit (non-inherited) ACE in its DACL.

The `acl` field returns all explicit ACEs as comma-separated entries in the format
`type:trustee:permissions`, where:

- **type** is `allow` or `deny`
- **trustee** is the resolved account name (e.g., `BUILTIN\Administrators`, `NT AUTHORITY\SYSTEM`)
- **permissions** is one of `full`, `modify`, `rx`, `read`, `write`, or a hex value for non-standard masks

Example output: `allow:BUILTIN\Administrators:full,allow:NT AUTHORITY\SYSTEM:full,allow:BUILTIN\Users:rx`

    fselect name from C:\ where has_acl = true
    fselect "name, acl from C:\Users where has_acl = true"

#### Extended file attributes

**fselect** can read and query extended file attributes (also known as file flags) that are managed
with `chattr` and displayed with `lsattr`. This feature is available only on Linux and works
on ext2/ext3/ext4, btrfs, and other filesystems that support the `FS_IOC_GETFLAGS` ioctl.

The `extattrs` field returns a string of flag letters for each set attribute, using the same
single-letter codes as `lsattr`/`chattr`:
`s` (secure deletion), `u` (undelete), `c` (compress), `S` (synchronous updates),
`i` (immutable), `a` (append only), `d` (no dump), `A` (no atime updates),
`E` (encrypted), `I` (indexed directory), `j` (journal data), `t` (no tail-merging),
`D` (dirsync), `T` (top of directory hierarchy), `e` (extents), `V` (verity),
`C` (no copy-on-write), `x` (DAX), `N` (inline data), `P` (project hierarchy),
`F` (case-insensitive directory).

The `has_extattrs` field returns true when any of these attributes are set.
Use the `has_extattr()` function to check for a specific flag:

    fselect name from / where has_extattrs = true
    fselect "name, extattrs from /data where has_extattrs = true"
    fselect "name from / where has_extattr('i')"
    fselect "name, extattrs from /data where has_extattr('a')"

    fselect size, path from /home/user/tmp where size gt 2g
    fselect fsize, path from /home/user/tmp where size = 5mib
    fselect hsize, path from /home/user/tmp where size lt 8kb

### Search roots

    path [option N] [option] [option] [option...][, path2 [option...]]

When you put a directory to search at, you can specify some options.

| Option         | Meaning                                                                                                                                                                             |
|----------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| mindepth N     | Minimum search depth. Default is unlimited. Depth 1 means skip one directory level and search further.                                                                              |
| maxdepth N     | Maximum search depth. Default is unlimited. Depth 1 means search the mentioned directory only. Depth 2 means search mentioned directory and its subdirectories. Synonym is `depth`. |
| symlinks       | If specified, search process will follow symlinks. Default is not to follow. Synonym is `sym`.                                                                                      |
| archives       | Search within archives. Only zip archives are supported. Default is not to include archived content into the search results. Synonym is `arc`.                                      |
| gitignore      | Search respects `.gitignore` files found. Synonym is `git`.                                                                                                                         |
| hgignore       | Search respects `.hgignore` files found. Synonym is `hg`.                                                                                                                           |
| dockerignore   | Search respects `.dockerignore` files found. Synonym is `dock`.                                                                                                                     |
| nogitignore    | Disable `.gitignore` parsing during the search. Synonym is `nogit`.                                                                                                                 |
| nohgignore     | Disable `.hgignore` parsing during the search. Synonym is `nohg`.                                                                                                                   |
| nodockerignore | Disable `.dockerignore` parsing during the search. Synonym is `nodock`.                                                                                                             |
| dfs            | Depth-first search mode.                                                                                                                                                            |
| bfs            | Breadth-first search mode. This is the default.                                                                                                                                     |
| regexp         | Use regular expressions to search within multiple roots. Synonym is `rx`.                                                                                                           | 

### Operators

* `=` or `==` or `eq`
* `!=` or `<>` or `ne`

* `>` or `gt`
* `>=` or `gte` or `ge`
* `<` or `lt`
* `<=` or `lte` or `le`
